facts.text: Tiger Hill (Huqiu) is a hill in Suzhou said to look like a crouching tiger; legend says a white tiger guarded King Helu's tomb.
A 48 m, seven-storey octagonal brick pagoda stands on the hill and is nicknamed the Leaning Tower of China.

suzhou-2.notes: Wikivoyage lists the Tiger Hill Pagoda at CNY 70 (60 off-season). A 2026 guide (citiesinsider) says 80/60; conflict, Wikivoyage used. No official site found via search (only third-party/OTA).

facts.text: Master of the Nets Garden is a small classical garden founded in 1140 and rebuilt in 1770, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Its house and garden complex is among the smallest and best proportioned in Suzhou; some evenings have traditional performance demonstrations.

suzhou-4.notes: Wikivoyage CNY 40; no official site found.

facts.text: Canglang Pavilion (Surging Wave Pavilion) is one of Suzhou's oldest scholar gardens, part of the UNESCO-listed Classical Gardens of Suzhou.
It is more densely forested than other Suzhou gardens, with pavilion windows framing the views.
Pingjiang Road is a historic street and district in the old town of northeastern Suzhou.
It is a walk along a road paved with hand-cut stones over a thousand years old, lined with shops in traditional style.

suzhou-8.notes: Open public street with no gate; Wikivoyage lists no fee. Free inferred from it being a street (no source states "free" in words).

facts.text: Hanshan Temple (Cold Mountain Temple) is a Buddhist temple about 5 km west of Suzhou's old city, founded as Miaoli Puming Temple.
Established in the Liang dynasty (502-557); most buildings date from the Tang, apart from a later five-storey pagoda.

suzhou-10.ticketUrl_evidence: Wikivoyage official URL returned HTTP 444 to script; check in browser.
suzhou-10.notes: No price on Wikivoyage. Ctrip lists ~CNY 20 (18 on dahepiao 2024) but OTA/aggregator, not used. Cost held.

facts.text: Couple's Retreat Garden is a classical Suzhou garden built in the early 20th century, UNESCO-listed.
Many small garden rooms and covered walkways lead from view to view, so it is enjoyable in rain.
Garden of Cultivation is one of the best-preserved Ming dynasty classical gardens in Suzhou, UNESCO-listed.
The best part is at the back of the garden.
Xuanmiao Temple (Temple of Mystery) is a prominent Taoist temple at the centre of old Suzhou.
Founded in the 3rd century and enlarged in the Song dynasty, it has a market area of small shops around the hall.

suzhou-16.ticketUrl_evidence: Wikivoyage url szxmg.com now shows a "domain for sale" page; not official.

facts.text: Jinji Lake is a 7.18 km2 freshwater lake in the centre of Suzhou Industrial Park with two man-made islands.
Ligongdi is a 1,400 m causeway across the lake, with metro stations nearby.

suzhou-18.notes: Lake shore and Ligongdi causeway listed on Wikivoyage with no fee. Evidence "pass list unreadable" is an NT template error; irrelevant to China.

facts.text: Suzhou Ferris Wheel is a 120 m wheel on the east bank of Jinji Lake with 60 cabins; a rotation takes about 20 minutes.

suzhou-20.notes: Single 2026 guide (Cities Insider) gives adult CNY 99, concession 60. Not on Wikivoyage. No official site found; tickets sold via WeChat mini-program.

facts.text: Suzhou Silk Museum, established 1991, documents silk production and Suzhou embroidery from around 2000 BC.
Exhibits include old looms with demonstrations and samples of ancient silk patterns.

suzhou-22.ticketUrl_evidence: Wikivoyage official URL unreachable from scripts (fetch failed, status 0); retry in browser.
suzhou-22.notes: Two guides (travelchina.frii.site, a Trip.com note) say free; one older listing says CNY 15. Free used, low confidence.

facts.text: Suzhou Confucian Temple, founded 1035 under Song dynasty, was China's first temple school and houses the Suzhou Stele Inscription Museum.
It holds four great Song dynasty steles, including a rare stone astronomical chart.

suzhou-24.ticketUrl_evidence: verified: page loaded; title "苏州碑刻博物馆 苏州文庙管理所" (Stele Inscription Museum / Confucian Temple management office).
suzhou-24.notes: Wikivoyage lists Confucian Temple price Free.

facts.text: Suzhou Embroidery Research Institute is a museum, workshop for craftspeople and shop for Suzhou embroidery.
Suzhou embroidery has a history of about 2,000 years and is one of China's four great embroidery styles.

suzhou-26.notes: No Wikipedia article. Wikivoyage lists no price; cost held.

facts.text: Suzhou Pingtan Museum is dedicated to Pingtan, storytelling and ballad singing in the Suzhou dialect.
Visitors can attend live performances.

suzhou-28.notes: No Wikipedia article. Wikivoyage: "Ticket fee for shows" with no amount; general entry unknown. Cost held.

facts.text: Garden of Pleasance (Yi Yuan) is a classical garden in Suzhou.
It is a very small garden in the heart of downtown, a place for a cup of green tea.

suzhou-30.notes: Wikivoyage lists no price. Cost held.

facts.text: Precious Belt Bridge is a stone arch bridge where the Grand Canal meets Tantai Lake, about 6 km southeast of central Suzhou.

suzhou-32.notes: Not in Wikivoyage Suzhou; no price source. Cost held.

facts.text: City God Temple of Suzhou is a Chinese folk temple in the old city.

suzhou-34.notes: No Wikipedia article. Wikivoyage lists price Free; the bio source is thin (only a name and fee on Wikivoyage), needs one more source for the bio.

facts.text: Suzhou Archaeological Museum is one of Suzhou's newest museums, displaying artefacts from archaeological sites in the Suzhou area.

suzhou-36.ticketUrl_evidence: verified: page loaded; title "苏州考古博物馆".
suzhou-36.notes: No Wikipedia article. Wikivoyage lists no price; cost held (official site loaded but price not read).

facts.text: Zhouzhuang is a canal water town 30 km southeast of Suzhou, within Kunshan.
Famous sights are Double Bridge (Twin Bridges), Fu'an Bridge, Shen's Residence and Zhang's Residence, with 14 stone bridges.

jiangnan-water-towns-1.ticketUrl_evidence: verified: page loaded; title "Jiangsu Shuixiang Zhouzhuang Tourism Co., LTD"; linked from Wikivoyage Zhouzhuang as the tourism website.
jiangnan-water-towns-1.notes: Price conflict, cost held: Wikivoyage prose says entry CNY 160 (likely stale); Ctrip shows 100 and a 2025 The Paper report says 50 on weekdays; none official.

facts.text: Luzhi is a historic canal town in Wuzhong District, 18 km east of Suzhou.
Baosheng Temple in the town is one of the top four Buddhist temples of the Jiangnan region.

jiangnan-water-towns-3.notes: No Wikivoyage page. Ctrip/Qunar say the town streets are free and sights ticketed (joint ticket); aggregator only, so cost held. Official site luzhi.com unreachable.

facts.text: Retreat & Reflection Garden in Tongli, Wujiang, is a classical garden recognised as UNESCO World Heritage in 2001.
It is the only one of the nine Suzhou classical gardens on the UNESCO list located outside downtown Suzhou.

jiangnan-water-towns-5.notes: Cost held: guides conflict (50 vs 100), may be included in the Tongli town ticket. Candidate official site http://www.tongli.net (title "同里古镇官方网站", names Tongli town, not the garden), so not used as ticketUrl.

facts.text: Baosheng Temple is a Buddhist temple in Luzhi town, Wuzhong District, Suzhou.
It is called one of the top four Buddhist temples of the Jiangnan region.

jiangnan-water-towns-7.notes: Ctrip shows ~CNY 80/59 (aggregator, not used). Cost held.

facts.text: Kunshan Opera Museum (Kunqu and hundred-operas museum) is in Kunshan.

kunshan-opera-museum.ticketUrl_evidence: verified: page loaded; title "戏曲百戏博物馆官网" (opera / hundred-operas museum official site), linked from Wikivoyage.
kunshan-opera-museum.notes: No Wikipedia article. Wikivoyage price Free. Bio fact is thin; needs another source (Chinese pages on the site not read).

facts.text: Zheng He Park in Taicang is a memorial park dedicated to Zheng He.
It includes a museum and a replica of a treasure ship; Taicang was the base of Zheng He's voyages to the West.

zheng-he-park-taicang.notes: Wikivoyage CNY 30 (undated). No official site found.

facts.text: Yushan is a hill in northwest Changshu, 300 m high and 6.5 km long, said to look like a sleeping cow.
The Wikivoyage listing notes a Great Wall section halfway up, views of the city and Shang Lake, and an old temple at the top.

yu-mountain-changshu.notes: Wikipedia title "Yu Mountain" is an album; correct article is "Yushan (Changshu)". Wikivoyage lists Yu Mountain National Forest Park CNY 35. No official site found.

facts.text: Shajiabang is a tourist village in Changshu beside Yangcheng Lake, with a scenic area called Shajiabang Resort.
